final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor offered no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the claim by conceding the core compliance defect already identified: a material weakness affects a named launch use case, while the record still lacks evidence of required disclosure, approved pre-launch risk acceptance, or remediation. Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public guidance on documentation and monitoring may support an operational or governance argument for managed deployment, but they do not satisfy the internal policy requirement stated in the record. This is therefore a reframing of the same evidence, not a genuine evidentiary update. A caveated certification posture may be a business or governance preference, but on the admissible compliance record it remains noncompliant because the unresolved policy predicate is still unmet.
remaining_concerns: The loan modification support segment is a named launch use case and is therefore material under the provided policy text.
That same segment is named in two lender rollout commitments, which reinforces materiality and defeats the non-core framing.
The segment still misses target by 1.4 percentage points.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed remains open.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this gap.
No admissible evidence shows the gap was remediated and re-evaluated before certification.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the policy predicate for a material named launch use case.
